bib.title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "MIND2WEB: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web", Xiang Deng, Yu Gu, Boyuan Zheng, Shijie Chen, Samuel Stevens, Boshi Wang, Huan Sun, Yu Su (The Ohio State University). Venue as printed (p1): "37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks." Copy read: arXiv:2306.06070v3, 9 Dec 2023.

COVERAGE: 81,353 of 81,353 chars, all 24 pages, including references and appendices A-D. Figures were checked by caption and surrounding text only; I did not view the images.

CLAIMS
- claim: Whole-task success stays low even when step success is moderate. The best model per split reaches 7.1 / 5.1 / 2.9% task SR. Flan-T5XL gets 52.0 / 38.9 / 39.6% step SR.
  number: Flan-T5XL Step SR 52.0 / 38.9 / 39.6, SR 5.2 / 5.1 / 2.9; Flan-T5L cross-task SR 7.1
  setup: MindAct (DeBERTa top-50, then fine-tuned multi-choice Flan-T5). Cross-Task 252 tasks, Cross-Website 177, Cross-Domain 912. Offline snapshots, macro average, no CI.
  quote: "w/ Flan-T5XL 55.1 75 .7 52 .0 5.2 42.0 65.2 38.9 5 .1 42 .1 66.5 39.6 2 .9"; "w/ Flan-T5L 53.4 75.7 50.3 7.1 39.2 67 .1 35 .3 1 .1 39 .7 67 .2 37 .3 2 .7"; "the overall task success rate remains low for all models, as the agent often commits at least one error step in most cases."
  where: p7 Table 2; p8
- claim: Scoring is open-loop. Each step is graded on its own with the true history supplied, so a task "succeeds" if every step matches. The agent never lives with its own earlier errors.
  number: none
  setup: all Table 2 metrics
  quote: none needed for a number. Text: "Each step of the task is evaluated independently with the ground truth action history provided." "A task is regarded successful only if all steps have succeeded. It is therefore a stringent metric."
  where: p7
- claim: Replay against cached snapshots causes false negatives, because a valid path that was not cached fails at once. The authors concede this.
  number: none
  setup: offline evaluation
  quote: "the task will fail immediately if an action was not cached during data collection, potentially leading to false negatives due to the existence of multiple paths for completing the same task."
  where: p10
- claim: Equivalent elements on the same page are accepted through a heuristic, which was hand-checked on 100 instances. No error rate is given.
  number: 100
  setup: nearest clickable ancestor plus visible descendants; used in training and evaluation
  quote: "Manual checking on 100 instances where the heuristic identifies a top-level element other than the ground truth confirms the validity of the approach."
  where: p20
- claim: GPT-4 was scored on only 50 tasks per split and with top-10 candidates, a different setup from the other models.
  number: GPT-4 Step SR 36.2 / 30.1 / 26.4; SR 2.0 in each split
  setup: temperature 0, 3 demonstrations, text HTML. My arithmetic, not the paper's: 2.0% of 50 is one task.
  quote: "For GPT-4 we use 50 tasks for each setting with top-10 candidates due to limited budget."; "w/ GPT-4∗ 41.6 60 .6 36 .2 2 .0 35 .8 51 .1 30 .1 2 .0 37 .1 46 .5 26 .4 2 .0"
  where: p7 Table 2
- claim: On GPT-4's own 50-task subsets, Flan-T5XL still beats GPT-4 on step SR. The "on par" claim in the text is about element selection only.
  number: Flan-T5XL 47.9 / 33.3 / 34.6 vs GPT-4 36.2 / 30.1 / 26.4 (parentheses are full-set values)
  setup: 50-task subsets
  quote: "Flan-T5XL 47.9 (52.0) 33.3 (38.9) 34.6 (39.6)"; "GPT-4 36.2 30 .1 26 .4"; "The performance is on par with the tuned Flan-T5 models under Cross-Website and Cross-Domain settings for element selection"
  where: p22 Table 7; p8
- claim: The first big drop comes from reaching unseen websites. Unseen domains add almost nothing further, which the authors attribute to website design and interaction logic rather than domain.
  number: over 10% average step SR gap
  setup: Cross-Task vs Cross-Website and Cross-Domain
  quote: "All models perform best on the Cross-Task setting, with over 10% absolute gap (step SR) on average compared with Cross-Website and Cross-Domain settings"
  where: p8 (see PROBLEMS: GPT-3.5 is an exception)
- claim: The multi-choice formulation beats direct generation of the element by a wide margin, and generation gets near-zero task success.
  number: Generation Step SR 17.5 / 11.0 / 11.9, SR 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.4; DeBERTa classification Ele. Acc 26.8 / 21.6 / 24.5
  setup: generation baseline is Flan-T5B (220M); classification is DeBERTaB (86M, element only)
  quote: "Generation 20.2 52 .0 17 .5 0 .0 13 .9 44 .7 11 .0 0 .0 14 .2 44 .7 11 .9 0 .4"; "Classification 26.8 − − − 21.6 − − − 24.5 − − −"
  where: p7 Table 2
- claim: GPT-3.5 is weak with three demonstrations, partly because it tends to pick "None of the above". The authors say the comparison with fine-tuned models is unfair.
  number: Ele. Acc 20.3 / 19.3 / 21.6; Step SR 17.4 / 16.2 / 18.6; SR 0.8 / 0.6 / 1.0
  setup: gpt-3.5-turbo, temperature 0, 3 demonstrations, same multi-choice format
  quote: "w/ GPT-3.5 20.3 56 .6 17 .4 0 .8 19 .3 48 .8 16 .2 0 .6 21 .6 52 .8 18 .6 1 .0"; "Note that this is not a fair comparison with the Flan-T5 models, which are fine-tuned on the full training data."
  where: p7 Table 2; p8
- claim: The candidate filter sets a ceiling, because any target missed before the LLM stage cannot be selected.
  number: Recall@50 88.9 / 85.3 / 85.7; heuristic cleaning 1,135 to 580 elements at 94.7% recall
  setup: DeBERTa-v3-base; the 94.7% is on training data
  quote: "it achieves 88.9% / 85.3% / 85.7% Recall@50"; "reduces the average number of elements from 1,135 to 580, while still maintaining an overall recall of 94.7% for the target element in the training data."
  where: p7
- claim: The dataset covers real sites with high-level goals only, and its pages are far larger than in earlier benchmarks.
  number: 2,350 tasks, 137 websites, 31 domains, 1,135 elements per page, 7.3 actions per task
  setup: compared with WebShop's 38 elements and 11.3 actions
  quote: "MIND 2WEB 5 / 31 137 Real-worldwebsites 1,135 2,350 High-level 7.3"; "WebShop [40] 1 1 Simplifiedshopping websites 38 12,000 products High-level 11.3"
  where: p5 Table 1
- claim: The splits hold out progressively more, and training data is small.
  number: 912 / 177 / 252 test tasks; 1,009 train
  setup: Cross-Domain holds out Information and Service (73 sites); Cross-Website holds out 10 sites per remaining top-level domain; Cross-Task is a random 20% (69 sites)
  quote: "with 912 tasks from 73 websites"; "containing 177 tasks"; "resulting in 252 tasks from 69 websites"; "contains 1,009 tasks from 73 websites."
  where: p7
- claim: Author verification removed few tasks but changed many descriptions, which shows how much crowd labels needed fixing.
  number: 61 of 2,411 discarded; 390 descriptions refined; extraneous steps cut in 187
  setup: Mechanical Turk annotators, verified by the authors
  quote: "we discarded 61 out of the total 2,411 tasks. Among the 2,350 retained tasks, the task description was refined in 390 instances to better correspond with the demonstrated actions, while some extraneous steps were discarded in 187 instances."
  where: p5
- claim: Reshuffling the option groups changes scores little. This is the paper's only variance figure.
  number: Flan-T5XL 51.9±0.8 / 39.5±0.2 / 39.6±0.2; "standard deviation less than 1"
  setup: 5 seeds, Flan-T5 only; covers random grouping of options
  quote: "Flan-T5XL 51.9±0.8 39 .5±0.2 39 .6±0.2"; "with standard deviation less than 1 for all runs."
  where: p21 Table 5, D.1
- claim: Without fine-tuning, Flan-T5XL largely fails at selection.
  number: zero-shot 10.8 / 7.8 / 11.7 vs fine-tuned 52.0 / 38.9 / 39.6
  setup: Flan-T5XL
  quote: "Flan-T5XL Zero-Shot 10.8 7 .8 11 .7"; "Flan-T5XL Fine-Tuned 52.0 38 .9 39 .6"
  where: p21 Table 6
- claim: State-changing actions are recorded but never executed, using a "Click (Fake)" operation. Such outcomes therefore cannot be verified by state.
  number: none
  setup: annotation; e.g. posting a comment or scheduling an appointment
  quote: "It will be recorded the same as a normal Click but will not get executed in the browser."
  where: p19

LIMITS
- No end-state check. Success means matching one crowd demonstration, element by element and with token-level F1 on the operation, so this is golden-path grading. Equivalence is handled only within a page (C.1), not across alternative paths.
- No closed-loop or live run. The authors call live evaluation "a very promising direction" (p10), so "readily transferable to live websites" (p10) is not demonstrated.
- No repeated trials, pass@k or pass^k, and no CIs on Table 2. GPT runs are temperature 0 (Table 4). There are no token, latency or cost numbers, only "high operational cost" (p8).
- Authors' concessions (pp9-10): sites are predominantly English and US-used; MTurk annotators may skew web-proficient; MindAct is text only with no visual input; each page is encoded independently, so page dynamics are not modelled; single up-front goal with no conversation; safety covered only as discussion.
- Pop-ups and CAPTCHAs are deliberately removed from the action sequences (p19), and sites were chosen to have no access issues. Real-web noise is therefore partly filtered, despite the "real-world" framing.
- No inter-annotator agreement is reported. Verification is by one author, with uncertain cases going to the first author (p17).
- Not stated: whether Table 7's non-GPT-4 rows also use top-10 candidates, which matters for comparing them with GPT-4.
- Dated: 2023 models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Flan-T5), 3 demonstrations, top-5 options per prompt. The 2023 scores say nothing about later models.

BUILDS ON
- Multi-choice over generation: "Recent studies [10, 13]", Chung et al. 2022 and Gu, Deng, Su 2022 (p6).
- Cross-encoder: Reimers and Gurevych 2019. DeBERTa: He et al. 2021. Flan-T5: Chung et al. 2022.
- Offline cached evaluation: "Following recent works [5, 35]", Burns et al. 2022 and Sun et al. 2022 (p10).
- Prior web datasets: MiniWoB++ (Liu et al. 2018), World of Bits (Shi et al. 2017), WebShop (Yao et al. 2022), RUSS (Xu et al. 2021).
- Mobile: PixelHelp (Li et al. 2020), META-GUI (Sun et al. 2022), MoTIF (Burns et al. 2022).
- Generalization-level framing: Gu et al. 2021 is in the references ("Beyond I.I.D."), but I found no explicit credit in the text for the three levels.
- Already in the target note's sources: Yao 2022 (2207.01206), Ahn 2022 (2204.01691), Qin 2023 (2304.08354), all listed here as refs [40], [2], [27].

CODE
Action-prediction prompt tail (p23 Table 8):
"What should be the next action? Please select from the following choices (If the correct action is not in the page above, please select A. 'None of the above'):"
Answer format (p23): "Answer: C. / Action: SELECT / Value: Pickup"
Hyperparameters (p21 Table 4): "temperature:0, # demonstrations: 3"; "batch_size: 32, epoch: 5, learning_rate:3e−5" (DeBERTa)

FIGURES (not viewed; judged from captions and text)
- Fig 6, p8: "Step success rate per website grouped by the three splits: TestCross-Task, TestCross-Website and TestCross-Domain from left to right. Here we only show websites with more than three test tasks." Shows per-website spread and that the last two splits look alike, which a table average hides. Top candidate.
- Fig 2, p4: "A sample data instance of our dataset with the three components. Actions marked in red will result in a transition to a new webpage." Shows what a reference trajectory is: 10 (element, operation) pairs.
- Fig 3, p6: "The overall pipeline for MINDACT with a small ranking LM for candidate generation, and a large prediction LM for action prediction." Shows the two-stage filter.
- Fig 5, p6: "Illustration of action prediction with LLMs." Contrasts multi-choice with direct generation.
- Fig 1, p2: "Sample tasks and all domains featured in MIND2WEB." Shows domain breakdown and generalization pairs.
- Table 2 (p7) is the main result, but it is a table, not a figure.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction: Table 2 and other tables have split decimals ("52 .0"), and bold marks are lost. Quotes are verbatim. I mapped Table 2 columns from the header order, so confirm against the PDF before quoting a cell. Text inside Figs 1, 3, 4, 5 extracts as fragments, and Figs 3-4 interleave.
- Pages: printed page numbers match PDF pages.
- Internal inconsistencies (mine, from the paper's own numbers):
  (a) "All models perform best on the Cross-Task setting" (p8), but GPT-3.5 scores 18.6 Cross-Domain vs 17.4 Cross-Task on step SR (Table 2).
  (b) D.3 says "the relative performance across methods and splits remains the same" (p22), but Table 7 reverses order on the subsets: Flan-T5L 48.1 > Flan-T5XL 47.9 Cross-Task, and Flan-T5B 28.1 > Flan-T5L 27.6 Cross-Domain. The full-set order is XL > L > B in each.
  (c) Table 6 is captioned "element selection results", but its fine-tuned row (52.0 / 38.9 / 39.6) equals Step SR in Table 2, not Ele. Acc (55.1 / 42.0 / 42.1).
  (d) p4 cites "Figure 2" for the demonstration tool; the tool is shown in Figure 7.
- Embedded instructions: none aimed at a reader. Tables 3 and 8 contain the paper's own prompts for ChatGPT/GPT models. I treated them as data and did not follow them.
